objective: Admit selective memory-intervention recommendations only when a candidate reminder is bound to task, session, intent, source evidence, freshness, confidence, novelty, token, sensitivity, cooldown, and replay policies.

research_inputs.finding: Proactive memory is an intervention decision: a memory policy updates structured state and decides whether a concise memory-grounded reminder should influence the next action-agent decision or remain silent. Selective intervention is distinguished from passive retrieval and always-on injection.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a receipt-only selective intervention admission contract with trigger, confidence, novelty, provenance, token, sensitivity, cooldown, and replay controls.

research_inputs.finding: Efficient agents require bounded memory lifecycle management, trigger-driven maintenance, selective retrieval, structured memory, and controlled memory/tool invocation to balance correctness, latency, token cost, and retrieval ambiguity.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract uses deterministic budgets and policy gates without requiring a provider, model, retrieval backend, prompt injection, or tool invocation.

features: cooldown, intervention-count, freshness, generation, and replay fences
receipt-only selective recommendation with memory_retrieved=false and prompt_injected=false

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane admission overhead; excludes memory retrieval, prompt construction, model inference, tool invocation, external services, and production approval latency

limitations: The contract validates caller-supplied memory and evidence digests; it does not retrieve or independently verify memory content.
The contract admits a recommendation but does not inject a reminder into an agent context, execute a model, or measure behavioral state decay.
The benchmark does not establish long-horizon task success, token savings, latency improvement, memory quality, AGI capability, production efficacy, or Linux superiority.
No physical hardware, external reviewer, independent builder, live multihost environment, or production approval was exercised.

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the memory-intervention module, tests, benchmark, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain the intent-repair release tag
